ux.task: Bind an element to a record field, close the editor, come back tomorrow
ux.finding: The founder's uncommitted work makes bindings survive a reload ONLY in the standalone/localStorage editor. In the SHIPPING editor (a real site, siteId in the URL) they still do not. Autosave sends composer.exportProject() - which now carries cmsBindings - to tRPC sites.saveProject, whose input schema is a plain z.object listing version/pages/styles/assets/metadata/settings; Zod strips unknown keys, so cmsBindings never reaches the server. And BuildrikSyncProvider.loadProject rebuilds ProjectData field-by-field from site + page rows and never sets cmsBindings. So the user binds a heading to a record, sees the record's text on canvas, reloads, and the heading is loose again - still showing the record's text (see UX-C-13) but no longer following it, with nothing said. The prior finding MOD-A-03 is therefore only HALF stale: the map's blanket 'STALE - do not act on it' is itself wrong for the editor everyone actually ships.
ux.evidence: packages/shared/schemas/sites.ts:192-214 (editorSaveProjectSchema.projectData, no .passthrough()); server/services/sites.service.ts:488-540 (saveProjectFromEditor's typed param list has no cmsBindings); packages/editor/src/services/BuildrikSyncProvider.ts:293-338 (loadProject's returned literal); useComposerInit.ts:526 picks saveProject(siteId, snapshot) over composer.saveProject(); the working-tree fix itself: Composer.ts:622-633 (export), :567-572 (import), project.ts:60-65. Searched: 'cmsBindings', 'cms_bindings', 'bindings', 'passthrough', 'projectData'.
ux.fix: Decide one storage home for bindings and make both halves agree. Until they do, the editor must not present binding as a durable act: the inspector's Bound chip and banner should be able to say when a binding is session-only, and the topbar save indicator should not read 'Saved' over state that was dropped in transit.
ux.purpose: Content/CMS is where a site's structured data lives - collections, their field schema, their records - and where canvas elements are wired to that data so one design serves many rows.

ux.task: Delete or rename a collection you created by mistake
ux.finding: A user can create collections from three different places and can never remove or rename one. The Content panel's collection rows are plain navigation rows with no menu; there is no rename field, no '...' affordance, no delete anywhere in the product. The engine has deleteCollection and updateCollection, and the Content panel even subscribes to the delete event so it would refresh - nothing ever fires it from a user action. A test collection made while learning the feature is permanent, and it keeps appearing in the binding popover's collection list forever.
ux.evidence: ContentViews.tsx:171-200 (RootView rows: ListRow + a 'New collection' Row, no actions slot); CollectionManager.ts:154 deleteCollection has zero callers outside CollectionStorage; ContentTab.tsx:97 subscribes to EVENTS.CMS_COLLECTION_DELETED. Searched: 'deleteCollection', 'Delete collection', 'remove collection', 'collection:deleted', 'CMS_COLLECTION_DELETED', 'renameCollection', 'rename collection' - the only UI caller of updateCollection is ContentTab.tsx:311, which sets pageSlugPattern.
ux.fix: Give the collection row an overflow menu with Rename, Edit description and Delete. Delete must first count what depends on it - records, bound elements, dynamic pages - and name those counts in the confirmation, the way the media library already does for an asset.
ux.purpose: Content/CMS is where a site's structured data lives - collections, their field schema, their records - and where canvas elements are wired to that data so one design serves many rows.

ux.task: Hide a section unless a data value says otherwise
ux.finding: The Conditions screen offers a complete-looking flow - pick an element on the canvas, write path/operator/value, Add condition - and the result is invisible. Evaluating a condition writes an attribute, data-condition-hidden="true", onto the element. No stylesheet in the repo reacts to that attribute and no export step reads it, so the element stays fully visible on the canvas and on the published site. The condition is also evaluated exactly once, at the moment it is created; nothing re-evaluates it when the data changes. The panel's own copy promises 'shows or hides an element based on data'.
ux.evidence: DataManager.ts:482-491 sets/removes data-condition-hidden and nothing else; grep for 'data-condition-hidden' / 'condition-hidden' / 'conditionHidden' across packages/editor/src returns only those two lines plus DataManager.test.ts:383-395 (a green test over an inert attribute); updateElementWithBinding is called only from the three bind sites (DataManager.ts:388,414,436); the promise is in ContentViews.tsx:1101-1103.
ux.fix: Either make the condition actually hide the element in the canvas and the export, or take the Conditions screen out of the Content panel until it does. As it stands the user's mental model - 'I have hidden this' - is contradicted by every surface, including the live site.

ux.task: Publish a record and watch the page update
ux.finding: Flipping a record's Published switch changes nothing on the canvas. The engine emits a distinct event for publish and unpublish, and the two things that refresh bound elements - the binding manager's re-apply and the canvas preview hook - both subscribe only to content:created / content:updated / content:deleted. So the user publishes, the record list updates, the canvas keeps showing whatever it showed before, and the only way to see the change is an unrelated edit or a reload. This is the moment the whole feature is meant to pay off, and it is the moment nothing happens.
ux.evidence: CollectionManager.ts:317-323 emits CMS_CONTENT_PUBLISHED / _UNPUBLISHED instead of _UPDATED on a status change; CMSBindingManager.ts:75-77 listens to the three raw strings 'content:created', 'content:updated', 'content:deleted'; useCMSPreview.ts:123-124 listens to the same two. Searched the constants ('CMS_CONTENT_PUBLISHED'), the raw strings ('content:published', 'content:unpublished') and the optional-call form ('on?.(') - no listener anywhere.
ux.fix: Publish must be a visible state change: the bound elements re-resolve, and the panel confirms what happened ('Published - 3 elements updated'). If a re-resolve is expensive, say so with a pending state rather than leaving the canvas silently stale.

ux.task: Keep an unfinished record out of the live site
ux.finding: The Published switch does not govern what ships. When an element is bound to a record, export resolves the binding by querying the collection with no status filter, so a record the user deliberately left as a draft has its half-written copy embedded in the published HTML. Publishing runs by default in this resolving mode. The binding popover even lists draft records for selection and labels them 'draft' as if that were a safe choice. Meanwhile the same switch DOES gate dynamic page generation - so one control means two different things depending on which feature reads it.
ux.evidence: CMSBindingManager.ts:120-123 resolveBinding calls queryContent({collectionId, filter:{}}) with no status; CMSExportResolver.ts:82-90 resolveStatic uses it; ExportEngine.ts:700-713 defaults cmsMode to 'static'; BindingPopover.tsx:303 renders every record with kbd={rec.status}. Searched: 'status', 'published', 'queryContent', 'resolveStatic'.
ux.fix: Make one rule and show it. Either bound elements resolve published records only (and the popover greys drafts with the reason), or the record editor stops calling the switch 'Published' and calls it what it governs. Publish should also count draft records that are about to ship and say so before deploying.
ux.purpose: Content/CMS is where a site's structured data lives - collections, their field schema, their records - and where canvas elements are wired to that data so one design serves many rows.

ux.task: Show a list - one card per record - instead of hand-binding one element per record
ux.finding: The reason to build a CMS is that one design serves many rows, and that is the one thing no screen in the editor can do. Every binding is element-to-one-record: pick a collection, pick a field, pick a specific record. The repeater machinery exists in full - bind an element as a collection template, expand it with clones, wrap it in a template loop on export - and no UI reaches any of it. The inspector's property registry even declares a 'collectionPicker' control for data.collection; no component renders that type. A user with a 40-item menu must place and bind 40 elements by hand.
ux.evidence: CMSBindingManager.ts:208 bindCollection and DataManager.ts:394 bindCollection have no UI caller; engine/cms/index.ts:9 exports RepeaterRenderer, which nothing imports; propertiesRegistry.ts:47,875 declare the collectionPicker type and the data.collection entry - grep for 'collectionPicker' returns those two lines only. Searched: 'bindCollection', 'RepeaterRenderer', 'repeater', 'Repeat with collection', 'collectionPicker', 'data.collection'. Re-verified against MOD-A-01/A-02 - both still hold.
ux.fix: A repeater is the primary CMS screen, not an advanced one. Design the flow that starts from a selected container: 'Repeat this with...' -> pick a collection -> the container's children become field slots -> the canvas shows real rows. Until that exists, the Content panel is a data-entry tool with no output.

ux.screen: Content panel > record  vs  Records modal
ux.task: Add a record
ux.finding: There are two record editors and which one a user meets is an accident of which door they found. The Content panel gives a stacked form with an unsaved-changes bar, a Discard-changes confirmation on leaving, a delete confirmation that warns the delete cannot be undone, and a Published switch on the form. The command-palette modal gives a table with a per-row Publish/Unpublish button, an inline add/edit form with NO unsaved guard (switching the collection dropdown throws the form away), delete with NO confirmation at all, required fields marked with an asterisk (the panel marks nothing), and real date/select widgets the panel does not have. Neither is a superset. The same destructive action - delete this record - asks in one place and does not ask in the other.
ux.evidence: Panel: ContentViews.tsx:379-397 (delete ConfirmDialog), :393-401 (Discard-changes ConfirmDialog), :401-433 (savebar), :340-357 (plain labels, no required marker). Modal: CMSRecordsModal.tsx:164-173 remove() deletes immediately, :276-279 collection change calls setEditingId(null) with no guard, :448-453 FieldLabel prints a red asterisk for required, :223-235 select/multiselect widgets, :236 date input. Confirms MOD-A-21.
ux.fix: Keep one record editor. The panel drill-in is the right home (it is on the rail and it already guards the destructive paths); fold the table view into it as a wide/expanded mode and retire the modal, or make the modal the one editor and give the panel row a 'Open in table' action. Whichever survives must carry the confirmations and the required markers.

ux.task: Add the first record and publish it in one go
ux.finding: Creating a record with the Published switch on, when a required field is empty, leaves a hidden duplicate behind every time the user retries. The save path creates the record as a draft first, then flips its status - and that second step is what runs validation and throws. The form catches the error and marks the fields, but the draft it already created stays, and the view still thinks it is composing a NEW record. Fix the field, press Save again, and a second draft is created. A user who fumbles a required field three times ends up with three drafts and one published record, and discovers it only when the collection list shows four rows.
ux.evidence: useContentPanel.ts:161-168 (createContentItem then updateContentItem({status}) - the second call throws); CollectionManager.ts:301-307 (validation runs only on the publish transition); ContentViews.tsx:414-424 (the catch marks fields and leaves the form open); ContentTab.tsx:262-266 (view.recordId stays null because setView is after the await).
ux.fix: Validate before writing anything, or keep the id of what was created and switch the form to editing it. Either way the user must never be able to produce a record they did not intend and cannot see.

ux.task: Generate one page per record
ux.finding: The Dynamic pages screen tells the user exactly what is wrong and gives them no way to fix it. It warns 'No template page is bound, so publishing emits none of these yet' - and the only control on the screen is the URL pattern. The template path, the SEO title and the SEO description can be set ONCE, inside the create-collection wizard, and never again; there is no edit path for any of them. A user who created the collection without turning on 'Generate a page per entry' can set a pattern here forever and publish zero pages. The wizard's own template field is free text with a sample path as a placeholder - no page picker, no validation that the path exists.

Searched: 'pageTemplatePath', 'pageSeoTitle', 'template page', 'templatePath'.
ux.fix: Put the template binding on this screen, as a picker over the site's real pages, and let SEO patterns be edited here too. A screen that states a blocking condition must own the control that clears it.

ux.screen: Content panel > Fields  /  Create collection wizard
ux.task: Fix a field you named wrong, or reorder the form
ux.finding: Fields can be added and deleted and nothing else. There is no rename, no type change, no way to turn 'required' on or off after the fact, and no reordering - so a typo in a field name is permanent unless the user deletes the field, which the confirmation correctly warns destroys that field's value on every record. ux.task: Delete a record that is already on a page
ux.finding: Deleting a record silently blanks every element bound to it. The delete fires a content:deleted event, the binding manager re-applies every binding, the deleted record no longer resolves, and because these bindings are created with no fallback the resolved value is an empty string - which is written straight onto the element. The confirmation says '"X" will be removed. This one can't be undone' and says nothing about the pages that were showing it. The editor already knows how to do this properly: deleting a media asset counts its usages first.
ux.evidence: CollectionManager.ts:328-337 emits CMS_CONTENT_DELETED; CMSBindingManager.ts:77 -> reapplyAll -> :162-181 applyBinding calls element.setContent(value) with no empty-value guard, while the preview and export paths both guard with `if (!value) return` (useCMSPreview.ts:64, CMSExportResolver.ts:85); BindingPopover.tsx:161-167 binds with five arguments, so `fallback` is undefined; the confirmation is ContentViews.tsx:384-386. Compare MediaCommandLayer.ts:326 getUsages. Searched: 'getUsages', 'usages', 'whereUsed', 'findUsages' - nothing equivalent for CMS.
ux.fix: Count the bound elements before deleting and put the number in the confirmation ('used by 3 elements on 2 pages'). When a binding cannot resolve, the element should fall back to visible placeholder copy and the inspector should flag it - not go blank.

ux.task: Bind an image on the page to a collection's Photo field
ux.finding: The popover offers every field type, including Image, and always binds the same thing: the element's text content. So binding an Image element to a Photo field writes the URL into the element's content instead of its src, and the picture never changes. The binding manager has correct handling for src, href, alt and title; no UI ever asks for them. There is also nothing stopping the user from binding a container or a section, where replacing the content is not a small mistake. Related: binding also overwrites whatever the element said before, and unbinding does not put it back - 'Unbind to type here' leaves the record's text sitting in the element permanently, and the binding is explicitly outside undo.
ux.evidence: BindingPopover.tsx:161-167 passes the literal "content" as the property, unconditionally; CMSBindingManager.ts:168-181 applyBinding maps content -> setContent and src/href/alt/title -> setTrait; the popover is mounted in the inspector header for every element type (ProInspector.tsx:382-386); BaseBindingManager.ts:106,125,134 note the bind and the unbind as unrecorded actions, so Cmd+Z cannot restore the original copy. Searched: '"src"', 'setTrait', 'property', 'bindToField'.
ux.fix: Ask which property to bind, defaulted from the element type and the field type (image field on an image element -> src). Offer only the fields that can drive the selected element. Keep the element's original content as the binding's fallback so unbind restores it and a missing record shows something.

ux.task: Put a photo on a product record
ux.finding: An Image field is a plain text box in both record editors. The user is expected to know a URL by heart; the editor's own media library - which they just used to place images on the canvas, and which the shell can open on demand - is not offered. The records table is honest about the result: an image cell reads '- missing' until some string is typed in. Same for date and select fields in the Content panel, which render as free text there and as real widgets in the modal.

ux.task: A viewer opens the site and looks at the content
ux.finding: No CMS surface knows about roles. The editor has a role service and uses it to gate Publish and Review, and its stated rule is that denied controls are shown disabled with the reason attached. The Content panel, both record editors, the create-collection wizard and the binding popover check nothing: a VIEWER can create a collection, add fields, type records, publish and delete them. Every one of those writes to local storage first and mirrors to the server second, so the work appears to succeed and then produces a toast that says the change is 'saved on this device but not yet on the server' with a Retry button - which is the wrong explanation and an action that can never succeed.
ux.evidence: RoleService.ts:1-41 (WorkspaceRole, roleAtLeast, and the 'disabled with the reason attached' rule); consumers are PublishTab.tsx, ReviewTab.tsx, StudioHeader.tsx, lifecycle.ts only; useCmsSync.ts:59-82 is the toast the viewer will get. Searched 'siteRole', 'canPublish', 'VIEWER', 'roleAtLeast', 'readonly', 'permission' under editor/sidebar/tabs/content/, CMSRecordsModal.tsx, CMSCollectionSetupModal.tsx and BindingPopover.tsx - no hit.
ux.fix: Gate the write controls on role the way Publish already is, and distinguish 'you cannot do this' from 'this did not reach the server'. A permission failure must not be reported as a network failure with a retry.

ux.task: Paste some JSON as a data source and use it
ux.finding: Data sources are not saved anywhere. They live in an in-memory map for the life of the tab: the project payload has no field for them and the data manager writes to no store. So a user pastes their JSON, sees the source row appear with a green dot and a 'Watching for changes' pill, reloads, and the Sources screen is empty again. Anything built on top of a source - every Condition, every {{site.*}} path - silently stops resolving at that moment, while the Conditions list still shows the rules as if they were live.
ux.evidence: ProjectData in shared/types/project.ts:30-66 has no data-source field; DataManager holds `sources` as a Map with no persistence (grep for 'localStorage', 'persist', 'save' inside engine/data/DataManager.ts returns nothing); the pill is ContentViews.tsx:773-784. Searched: 'dataSources', 'exportData()', 'registerSource', 'localStorage'.
ux.fix: Persist sources with the project, or stop presenting them as a saved thing: no 'Watching for changes' pill and an explicit note that a source lasts for this session. If they are meant to feed the published site, they need to travel with it.

ux.task: Re-import a JSON file after editing it
ux.finding: Importing JSON whose top-level key already exists as a source throws, and the panel reports it as 'Not valid JSON - check the syntax and try again.' The user's JSON is perfectly valid; the real problem is a name collision, and the fix - remove the old source first - is never mentioned. The catch is a bare `catch` around the whole import, so every failure mode gets the syntax message. This is the most likely second action on the screen: paste, correct the data, paste again.

ux.fix: Detect the collision and offer the choice the user wants - replace the existing source, or import under a new name. Reserve the syntax message for an actual parse error.

ux.finding: Nothing outside the Content panel knows dynamic pages exist. The Pages panel - the place a user goes to see their site's pages - has no concept of a collection, a pattern or a generated route: its files contain no reference to any of it. The Publish surfaces are the same: the publish tab, the pre-publish facts and the publish confirmation mention no collection, no record, no draft count and no generated page. ux.task: Fill in the first step of the wizard
ux.finding: Step 1 asks for a Content type - Articles, Products, Team Members, Custom - and the answer is thrown away. It is never read when the collection is created: no preset fields, no icon, no behaviour changes. A user who picks 'Products' expecting product fields gets an empty collection with whatever they type on step 2. The same step lets a collection be created with zero fields (Create is enabled on the name alone, and every field row can be deleted), and there is no check for a name that already exists - two collections called 'Blog' both slugify to 'blog' and become indistinguishable in the binding popover's list.

ux.task: Get a hundred rows in, or get your content back out
ux.finding: Records go in one at a time, by hand, and never come out. There is no CSV or JSON import for records, no export, and no bulk edit - the modal's own code notes that the Import JSON button its board draws was left unbuilt because the engine creates one record at a time. For the stated purpose of the feature - 'Collections turn a spreadsheet into pages' - the spreadsheet has no way in. A restaurant with a 40-item menu types 40 records through a form.
ux.evidence: CMSRecordsModal.tsx:426-432 (the note explaining Import JSON was not built); the empty-state promise is ContentViews.tsx:150 and CMSCollectionSetupModal.tsx:293-295. Searched 'csv', 'importContent', 'exportContent', 'bulk' across engine/cms/, the content panel and the records modal - the only hit is CollectionStorage.ts:221 deleteAllContentItems, which no UI calls either.
ux.fix: Paste-a-table or upload-a-CSV into a collection, with a column-to-field mapping step, and an export of the same shape. This is the difference between a demo CMS and one someone moves a real site into.

ux.task: Find one record among two hundred
ux.finding: Neither record view can be searched, filtered, sorted or paged. The panel renders every record in the collection as a row in a 320px column; the modal renders every record as a table row and shows only the first three fields, with no indication that the rest exist. There is no status filter, so there is no way to answer 'which of my records are still drafts' - the question the publish flow makes urgent (UX-C-05). The engine's own query API supports filter, sort, limit and offset; no screen uses any of it.

ux.task: Create a collection from the moment you realise you need one
ux.finding: '+ Create Collection' at the foot of the binding popover closes the popover, opens the wizard, and abandons the user there. The wizard auto-closes about a second after success and nothing reopens the popover or reselects anything - the user has to find the chain icon again. And because the new collection has no records, reopening the popover reaches the 'No records yet' dead end (UX-C-10) rather than a finished binding. The one gesture that starts from a real need takes the longest route to nothing.

ux.task: Press Undo just after opening a site that has bindings
ux.finding: Restoring bindings at load counts as an unrecorded change, so the first thing a freshly opened site does is disable Undo - and if the user presses Cmd+Z before their first edit, the refusal blames 'binding a field to content', an action they did not perform. It corrects itself on the first real edit, so the damage is confusion rather than loss, but the message names the wrong culprit at the one moment a user is most likely to be trying to undo something they think went wrong.

ux.finding: Every list of records - the panel, the table, the binding popover - labels a row with the collection's display field, falling back to the first field and then to 'Record 4f2a'. summary.finding:
PURPOSE. Content/CMS exists so a site's repeating, changing information - menu items, posts, products, team members - lives as structured records instead of as typed-in copy, and so a page follows those records rather than being edited whenever they change.

PRIMARY TASKS. (1) Create a collection and define its fields. (2) Add, edit, publish and delete records. (3) Bind a canvas element to a record's field. (4) Generate one page per record from a URL pattern. (5) Register data sources, site variables and element conditions from the same panel's Data group.

ENTRY POINTS. The Content rail item (RAIL_FIGMA, tabsConfig.ts:250-260 - the default rail includes it); the command palette's 'Open Content panel'; the inspector's chain icon on every selected element (ProInspector.tsx:382); the command palette's 'Manage CMS records' (the records modal's ONLY door, useCanvasCommandPalette.ts:167); and an automatic prompt when an e-commerce block is inserted (useComposerInit.ts:764).

EXITS. Breadcrumb back through the drill-in stack to the panel root; the panel's close button; modal close. There is no exit from a collection to the pages it generates, none from a record to the elements bound to it, and none from a bound element to its record - the banner tells the user to 'Edit the record in Content' and does not link there (BindingBanner.tsx:89-91).

HANDS OFF TO. Canvas (useCMSPreview resolves bindings for display), Inspector (binding popover, bound chip, binding banner), Export/Publish (CMSExportResolver runs on every export by default, ExportEngine.ts:700-713), the dashboard server (cmsSync mirrors collections and entries), and Pages - in intent only; the Pages panel contains no reference to collections or dynamic pages.

RECEIVES FROM. Canvas selection (which element the binding popover acts on, and the element-pick used by Conditions); the e-commerce block insert; the server hydration on open (cmsSync.hydrateCmsFromServer -> refreshFromStorage); and the project load, which as of the working tree also restores element bindings.

STATE OF THE JOURNEY. A user can complete steps 1, 2 and 3 and cannot see the result: publishing a record does not refresh the canvas, one binding serves exactly one record because no repeater is reachable, and in the shipping editor the binding itself does not survive a reload. Steps 4 and 5 are described more completely than they are built - dynamic pages block on a template path the panel cannot set, and conditions write an attribute nothing reads.
summary.evidence: Composed from the rows above; every file:line in this summary appears in a row's evidence and was read directly. Working tree audited, not HEAD: git diff on Composer.ts, project.ts and engine/cms/ was read first.
summary.fix: Sequence the redesign around the one journey that must work end to end - collection -> fields -> records -> repeater on canvas -> publish - and give the collection a settings screen that owns rename, delete, display field and dynamic pages. Everything else in this lane is a consequence of that spine being absent.
summary.purpose: Content/CMS is where a site's structured data lives - collections, their field schema, their records - and where canvas elements are wired to that data so one design serves many rows.
